column1: # blobExec blob denylist — blobs excluded from the rewrite by content id.
# A denylisted blob is never handed to the tokenizer. It is dropped from every
# rewritten tree, exactly like an oversized blob (Walker.readBlob), so the file is
# ABSENT from the tokenized repository rather than present as raw source: it
# produces no blame and no dataset row. It is counted separately from
# blobsOversized and blobsTimedOut, logged once with its sha, path and reason, and
# it does NOT affect the exit status. That last point is the difference between
# this list and a timeout: an entry here is a diagnosed, deterministic, cited
# exclusion, while a timeout is a hang nobody has explained yet and must keep
# blocking publication.
# This is a DATA file, not a constant in the code, so a paper can cite the list
# itself. It is loaded from the classpath (BlobDenylist.ResourcePath) and shipped
# inside the assembly jar, so adding an entry means editing this file and running
# `sbt assembly`. Nothing at run time can extend or override it: an undocumented
# exclusion is the one thing that would make the dataset's omissions unauditable.
# FORMAT: three TAB-separated fields. Blank lines and lines starting with # are
# ignored. Leading and trailing whitespace on a field is stripped.
#     <git blob sha1, 40 lowercase hex>  <citation>  <one-line reason>
# The key is the GIT BLOB id, which is what the walker has in hand
# (Walker.BlobMissTask.origId) and what blobExec's own timeout line prints. It is
# not the memo's key: tokenizeByBlobId/tokenBySha.pl hashes the file contents
# alone, with no git object header.
# The key is deliberately NOT the path. Every entry below is one of THREE source
# files, at several historical versions and in one case at two paths after an
# OpenJDK repository reorganisation. A path-keyed list would have to be updated
# every time a project moves a file, and would not distinguish the versions of a
# file that hang from the versions that parse — which here is a 4/4 split on one
# of them. Content is the stable identity. The paths are recorded for a reader
# rather than matched on.
# EVERY entry is srcML 1.1.0 non-termination. But they are TWO DISTINCT
# DEFECTS, in TWO DIFFERENT LANGUAGES, with only one upstream issue between
# them. Do not read this list as one defect, and do not cite #2361 for class 2.
# CLASS 1 — the JAVA parser, on type-annotated array types.
#   Upstream: srcML/srcML#2361, open, no patch.
#   8 blobs, TWO files, both in tencent__tencentkona-21 (OpenJDK-derived,
#   50,663 .java files at HEAD, 147,265 blobs recorded). Both are OpenJDK
#   langtools regression tests whose stated purpose is to stress exactly the
#   grammar that breaks the parser: not production source, and carrying no
#   contributor-behaviour signal. That is what makes excluding them cheap.
#   TestNewCastArray.java  — @bug 8005681 "Repeated annotations on new,array,cast"
#     test/langtools/tools/javac/annotations/typeAnnotations/classfile/
#       2ee2673ad0a8ff2cef0254e7bfdc488cc1d61a65   14,503 B
#     langtools/test/tools/javac/annotations/typeAnnotations/classfile/
#       504aaf9109fc01d6d62d99ac529ded99a8dfa8ca   14,451 B
#   CheckErrorsForSource7.java  — @run main CheckErrorsForSource7
#     langtools/test/tools/javac/annotations/typeAnnotations/failures/
#       56c8adf588e697a3e42b600b2e5ec54710592c61    8,388 B   trigger at line 178
#       5e9c9138ed9c43c20591d1814cb72ad014d1a9e5    8,750 B   trigger at line 181
#       6bf666550f6cba72f1602ce1b7a6b0c9025fc8c7    8,645 B   trigger at line 179
#     test/langtools/tools/javac/annotations/typeAnnotations/failures/
#       afbd81e5789ba060147b0de3be4f01759963299d    8,617 B   trigger at line 178
#       (5e9c9138… lives at both paths; all four versions of the file hang)
# TestNewCastArray's trigger, minimised in srcml-nontermination-analysis.md, is a
# declaration whose declared type is a multi-dimensional array carrying a type
# annotation on its first dimension WHEN the initializer is an array-creation
# expression that also carries one:
#     String @A [] [] s = new String @A [2] [2];
# CheckErrorsForSource7 is a DIFFERENT FILE with a SECOND, DISTINCT sufficient
# construct in the same #2361 family, minimised here on 2026-09-20. It needs no
# initializer at all:
#     Object [] @TA [] arr @TA[];          // the real line
#     class C { int @A [] a @A []; }       // minimal reproducer, 31 B
# BOTH an annotated dimension in the declared type AND an annotated trailing
# C-style array dimension on the declarator are required; either one alone parses
# in under 90 ms, and it makes no difference whether the declaration is a field or
# a local, or whether an initializer is present. The neighbouring line 179,
# `<T> @TA int @TA[] ret(Object obj) @TA[]`, was measured and is NOT a trigger: on
# its own it parses in 8 ms. Offer this reproducer upstream on #2361 alongside the
# first one — it is a second sufficient condition the issue does not record.
# CLASS 2 — the C parser, on C++ inside a `.h`.
#   NO UPSTREAM ISSUE EXISTS. This is NOT #2361: different language, different
#   construct, separately minimised. The citation is the analysis document.
#   4 blobs, ONE file, in facebook__sapling. Unlike class 1 this is ordinary
#   production source, so the exclusion does cost real signal — 4 blobs of a
#   1.9-2.6 kB header, bounded below.
#   eden/fs/utils/StatTimes.h   (historical only; NOT present at HEAD)
#       dbb885e0bf046755c4fcfbddfc2454f90c550c62    2,442 B
# CregitLanguages.pm maps the `.h` extension to language C, so tokenBySha.pl runs
# `srcml -l C` over a header whose contents are C++. The C parser then does not
# terminate. Minimised on 2026-09-20 from 1,861 bytes to 41:
#     namespace n{struct T&f(const struct S);}
# Necessary and sufficient, each condition measured. Remove any one and the input
# parses in under 12 ms:
#   - an enclosing NAMED `namespace X {` or `class X {` block. An anonymous
#     `namespace {` does NOT trigger it.
#   - a return type that is a REFERENCE to an ELABORATED struct type, `struct T&`.
#     `struct T*` parses; `T&` without the `struct` keyword parses.
#   - a parameter of CV-QUALIFIED ELABORATED struct type, `const struct S`
#     (`volatile` does it too). The parameter need not be a reference and need not
#     be named. `const S` without `struct`, and `struct S` without the qualifier,
#     both parse.
# THE THREE BACKSLASH-CONTINUED `#elif defined(…) || \` CONDITIONALS AT LINES 24,
# 37 AND 50 ARE NOT THE TRIGGER. They are the file's most conspicuous feature and
# the obvious suspect, and they are innocent: extracted on their own they parse in
# 8 ms, and — the decisive evidence — this file has EIGHT historical versions, ALL
# EIGHT carry three or four such continued `#elif` conditionals, and only FOUR
# hang. The split is exactly the reference return type: the four that hang all
# declare `inline const struct timespec& stAtime(const struct stat& st)`, and the
# four that parse in milliseconds all return `struct timespec` BY VALUE. A natural
# experiment in the corpus's own history, 4/4, agreeing with the minimisation.
# The same 1,861 bytes parse as C++ in 9 ms and produce 14,125 bytes of srcML, so
# a `.hpp` name would never have hit this. That narrowness — C++ declared in a
# `.h`, named namespace, reference to an elaborated struct, cv-qualified
# elaborated struct parameter — is why 188 C and C++ projects produced ONE
# instance of this class rather than thousands.
# Blast radius, measured rather than assumed: a bounded probe of ALL 29,100
# mask-selected C/C++/Java blobs in facebook__sapling's whole history found these
# 4 and no others. 4 of 29,100 is 0.014%.
# WHY THIS IS NON-TERMINATION AND NOT SLOWNESS, for every entry
# Zero bytes of output, one core at 100%, and resident memory FLAT, at every
# budget tried. Flat memory with a saturated core rules out backtracking that
# would eventually finish and rules out memory exhaustion. Measured 2026-09-20
# against the pinned binary, reading the counters from the srcml CHILD and not
# from the `timeout` supervisor, which blocks in wait4 at 0% CPU and would look
# idle:
#   StatTimes.h    as C     5 s / 15 s / 60 s / 300 s   0 B out, 100%, RSS 9.2-9.4 MB
#   the other 3 .h as C    15 s / 60 s                  0 B out, 100%, RSS 9.3-9.4 MB
#   CheckErrors…   as Java 15 s / 60 s                  0 B out, 100%, RSS 10.1 MB
#   all 6 newly listed here                             also killed at 600 s in the
#                                                       pipeline, status 124 from
#                                                       `timeout` — not 137, not OOM
# srcML v1.1.0 (2025-08-14) is the latest release, so there is nothing to upgrade
# to. A working patch for class 1 was built and validated at 12,016/12,016
# byte-identical blobs and deliberately NOT adopted, on provenance grounds. Both
# write-ups, and the minimisation behind class 2, live in
# cregit-token-pipeline/.superpowers/sdd/peppy-pondering-music/ —
# srcml-nontermination-analysis.md, srcml-upstream-fix-adjudication.md and
# task-8c-finish-report.md.
# THIS LIST IS NOT THE COMPLETE SET OF NON-TERMINATING BLOBS IN THE CORPUS
# A THIRD class exists and is deliberately NOT listed here, because excluding it
# is a decision about the dataset's content rather than about a stress test: the
# C++ parser also fails to terminate on `src/hotspot/share/runtime/
# continuationFreezeThaw.cpp` in tencent__tencentkona-21 — ~105 kB of ORDINARY
# PRODUCTION SOURCE in the JVM runtime, 0 bytes out at 15 s and 120 s with the
# same flat-memory, one-core signature. Denylisting production source removes real
# contributor-behaviour signal, so it is escalated in task-8c-finish-report.md
# rather than decided in this file. Until that decision is taken,
# tencent__tencentkona-21 cannot complete step 2, and the timeout — which DOES
# block publication — is the correct thing to be stopping it.
# sha
